ios.desc:
Improve your chess skills with Knighty, the gamified chess puzzles app designed to make learning chess fun and addictive!


Master essential chess tactics through beautifully designed skill trees and progressive challenges. From basic forks and pins to complex checkmate patterns, Knighty puzzles helps us have fun and learning at the same time.


KEY FEATURES:
• Around 20,000 puzzles for all skill levels covering various themes
• Engaging skill tree progression system
• Daily challenges to maintain your streak
• XP system with rewards for consistent practice
• Interactive chess board with easy move validation
• Progress tracking and achievement badges
• Intuitive interface designed for chess learners


Whether you're a beginner learning chess fundamentals or an experienced player looking to sharpen your tactical skills, Knighty offers a fun, gamified approach to chess improvement.


Train your chess brain just minutes a day and watch your tactical vision improve dramatically. Build your streak, earn achievements, and climb the skill tree to become a true Chess Master!


Download now and start your journey to chess mastery!

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I've built an iOS app called Knighty Chess, designed for improving chess tactics through daily puzzles and structured learning, and I'd love to share it with you.

The app offers around 20,000 puzzles organized into skill trees, covering various tactical motifs from basic to more complex patterns. It includes daily challenges and tracks progress with XP, achievements and leaderboard.

You can check it out on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/knighty-chess/id6745241794
  This is my second project related to chess. Last year I built termichess , a terminal app to play chess which received a lot of  support from the HN community. 
This was a personal project, and I'm here to discuss it. I'm particularly interested in any feedback you might have on the puzzle selection, user experience, or any features you think would make it better for learning.

Thanks for taking a look
